Seasonal Fruit Offering Platter

Served at: Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana) · Dia de los Angelitos

One large platter (serves 4-6 as an offering)Prep 20 min

This Seasonal Fruit Offering Platter is a simple yet profound way to honor ancestors and spirits during the Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana) and Dia de los Angelitos. Fresh fruit symbolizes purity, abundance, and the bounty of the earth, making it a respectful and cherished offering. It's prepared with care to reflect devotion and remembrance.

Ingredients

  • 2-3 (500-750 g) ripe mangoes or papayas
  • 1 bunch (500 g) green or red grapes
  • 4-6 (600-900 g) medium apples or pears
  • 1 cup (150 g) fresh berries (strawberries, blueberries, or raspberries)
  • 2-3 (400-600 g) oranges or mandarins
  • Optional: 1/2 (250 g) cantaloupe or honeydew melon

Method

  1. Select a variety of fresh, ripe, and unblemished fruits. Choose fruits that are in season and appealing.
  2. Gently wash all fruits under cool running water. Pat them dry thoroughly with a clean cloth or paper towel.
  3. For larger fruits like mangoes, papayas, or melons, carefully peel them, remove any seeds or pits, and cut the flesh into manageable, bite-sized pieces or slices.
  4. For apples, pears, and oranges, you may slice them into wedges or rounds, or leave smaller fruits whole if preferred. Remove any cores or seeds.
  5. For smaller fruits like grapes and berries, leave them whole. If using strawberries, you may hull them.
  6. Arrange the prepared fruits artfully on a clean serving platter, a traditional offering plate, or a woven basket. Aim for a visually appealing display with a variety of colors and textures.
  7. Present the fruit platter as an offering on your altar or designated offering space, ensuring it is placed respectfully.

Tips

  • Choose fruits that are in season and locally available for the freshest taste and appearance, which also honors the local harvest.
  • A mix of colors (e.g., red apples, green grapes, yellow mangoes) makes the offering visually appealing and vibrant.
  • Ensure all fruits are thoroughly cleaned and free of any blemishes or imperfections, as this reflects deep respect for the ancestors and spirits.
